# Sample report

[`benchmark.report.html`](benchmark.report.html) is the HTML report PlasBench writes, built from the **offline demo dataset**. Open it in a browser (it is one
self-contained file; no server and no internet are needed), or view it online: [open the sample report](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/ubeffiong/plasbench/blob/main/docs/sample_report/benchmark.report.html).

**The data are synthetic.** The demo cohort (6 isolates, 5 tools) is generated by `test/demo_dataset.py` so the report can be shown and tested without downloading
anything. Its numbers are not results about any real tool, and nothing in it should be quoted as a finding. What it shows is how a real run is presented: the
Overview, the recommendation, the figures, the plasmid maps, the detailed tables, the data-quality checks and the limits, with a green **?** button on every section
and tab that explains the analysis in plain language.

Two things differ from a real run:

- The report links to files of its results folder (tables, maps, selected FASTA files). Those 549 files are not included here, so those links open only when the
  report sits beside its results folder, as it does after a run.
- Large optional parts are included so every feature can be seen (the interactive cohort dashboard and the evidence explorer).

## Regenerate it

```bash
bash test/run_demo.sh                                   # writes results_demo/benchmark.report.html (about 2 minutes)
cp results_demo/benchmark.report.html docs/sample_report/benchmark.report.html
```

`test/test_sample_report.py` checks that the sample exists, carries the help dialog and no local paths, and that the README links to it. Regenerate it when the report
changes in a way you want the sample to show; the file is about 11 MB, so regenerate it deliberately, not on every commit.
